item.text:
This turn closed the loop on finding 3's mechanism and recorded the trace evidence.

**Instrumented stall trace (diagnostic core copy).** I fixed the prepared copy (had to clone `omnipaxos_storage` too and rename both packages, keeping lib names) and added tracing to `resend_messages_leader`, `resend_messages_follower` and `handle_sequence_num` — nothing else changed. Two of three runs stalled at 122.91 s, and the trace shows:

- the leader sat for the whole stall at `accepted_idx=9 decided_idx=9 accepted_indexes=[5, 9, 10]`, i.e. it *knew* a follower was at accepted 5 while it had 9, and its only resend was the StopSign `Decide`;
- the follower those resends went to dropped every one of them, right to the end: `msg=(session 3, counter 1) current=(session 3, counter 1) -> Outdated`. That is exactly the source-level prediction (`send_decide(.., resend=true)` reuses the counter the follower has already consumed) seen directly in a run;
- one node stopped ticking after ~6 resend periods — the node the test itself stops to block the write quorum and never restarts.

I explicitly recorded what that trace does **not** settle: mapping the panic's "Follower log" (decided 5) onto a pid. The pids visible in the trace sit at accepted 10/decided 9 and stopped-at-3, so the final link in *that* harness is implied rather than observed end-to-end. The finding itself does not rest on it — the deterministic probe (drop the accept and the decide; follower stays at `accepted = decided = 0` for 5000 rounds; a single `reconnected(1)` fixes it) shows the gap directly, and it is what the report leads with.

Along the way I also had to correct myself: my first mechanism guess (any single lost `AcceptDecide` strands a follower) was disproved by tracing the message flow — the leader's later `Decide` carries the next counter, the follower classifies it `DroppedPreceding`, and it resyncs itself. Both the refutation and the surviving mechanism are in the report.

Current state of the audit: three findings (two runtime-layer with deterministic repros, one core liveness defect with repro, remedy, and instrumented stall evidence), a large negative-result set (crash-recovery `#[ignore]`d tests pass when run, stale-leader adoption, 4000-round partition/churn soak, StopSign boundary, unicache and workspace sweeps), corrected baseline counts, evidence-base caveats, and a short open list. Everything is in [report.md](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-16_23-10-28-omnipaxos-baseline/work/report.md) with reproduction commands and logs under `work/notes/`.
